mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production and housing starts indicate strong supply and demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Both series increase but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening cycle, higher FEDFUNDS leads to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs rise.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: High CPI indicates inflation, leading to potential rate hikes and negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: CPI is high but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth over 0.5% signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales and falling unemployment indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Both series improve but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, low unemployment may signal overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Unemployment below 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive.
